key_insight: Non-binary detector error models preserve each circuit fault’s original Pauli alphabet, representing arbitrary Pauli channels exactly while enabling more compact decoding graphs.
engineering_relevance: Tanner graphs with four to five times fewer edges could simplify decoder hardware, while BP with OSD post-processing achieved up to 9.4× CPU speedup in reported tests.
method: Model each fault location as one random variable over its original error alphabet.
Apply split-merge-regroup to merge components with identical detector and observable flips.
Decode using belief propagation with one scalar message per edge, optionally followed by OSD.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on surface, color and bivariate bicycle codes showed better BP performance, with and without OSD, than binary counterparts.
watch_item: Binary and non-binary models are proven equivalent only for factorizing channels under degenerate quantum MAP decoding, not under quantum MAP decoding.
